category: 3D & MCAD, rigid-flex, panelization and PCB footprint libraries
description: The mechanical and library side of the Altium PCB editor: the 3D view and STEP/Parasolid model handling, collision and clearance checking against an enclosure, MCAD co-design, rigid-flex board regions and bending lines, embedded board arrays and panelisation, and the PCB Library editor with its footprint wizards and 3D bodies.

tools.name: Switch to 3D / 2D view
tools.description: Toggles the PCB editor between the 2D layout view and the fully rendered 3D view, in which the board, its copper, masks, silkscreen and all attached 3D bodies are shown. Numeric 3 switches to 3D, 2 back to 2D, and 1 gives the 2D board planning mode. In 3D, Shift plus the right mouse button rotates and the wheel zooms.
tools.usage: View > Switch To 3D (3) / Switch To 2D (2) / Board Planning Mode (1); Shift + right-drag to rotate
tools.example: Press 3, Shift+right-drag to look along the board edge, and check that the tall electrolytic clears the lid.
tools.notes: Some scripting operations (and a few commands) only work in 2D; a script can force the mode with `RunProcess('PCB:SwitchTo2D')`.

tools.name: 3D Body
tools.description: The object that gives a footprint or a board its 3D shape. A 3D body can be an Extruded shape from a drawn outline, a Cylinder, a Sphere or a Generic STEP model loaded from file; its height, standoff, colour, opacity and snap points are set in the Properties panel. Bodies live on a mechanical layer and are what collision checking and STEP export work with.
tools.usage: Place > 3D Body (P,B in the PCB library editor); Properties panel to choose the model type and file

parameters.name: 3D Model Type
parameters.description: Extruded, Cylinder, Sphere or Generic STEP Model.

parameters.name: Overall Height / Standoff Height
parameters.description: Body height and how far it sits above the board surface.

parameters.name: Snap Points
parameters.description: Points used to align an imported STEP model to the footprint's pads and origin.

parameters.name: Layer
parameters.description: Mechanical layer the body belongs to, which controls which side it is on when the component is flipped.

tools.example: In the PCB Library editor: Place > 3D Body > Generic STEP Model > browse to connector.step > use Tools > 3D Body Placement > Add Snap Points From Vertices to align it to pin 1.
tools.notes: A footprint with no 3D body still shows an extruded courtyard block in 3D, which is enough for height checks but not for mating or fit.

tools.name: 3D Body Manager
tools.description: Lists every 3D body used on the board or in the library with its source model, and manages the links: re-pointing a model to a new file, embedding or referencing external STEP files, and reporting bodies whose model is missing. It is the place to audit a board's 3D completeness before an MCAD handover.
tools.usage: Tools > Manage 3D Bodies For Components / Manage 3D Bodies for Current Component (PCB and PCB Library editors)
tools.example: Tools > Manage 3D Bodies For Components > filter for components with no body > add STEP models for the missing ones.

tools.name: STEP / Parasolid model import
tools.description: Brings mechanical geometry in. A STEP (.step/.stp) or Parasolid (.x_t/.x_b) file can be loaded as a Generic 3D Body for a component, or placed on the board as the enclosure, heatsink or mating part so clearance can be checked in context. Imported models are positioned with snap points and the 3D body's rotation and offset fields.
tools.usage: Place > 3D Body > Generic STEP Model > Embed STEP Model / Link to STEP Model; or File > Import > STEP into a mechanical layer
tools.example: Place a 3D body on Mechanical 16 with the enclosure's STEP file so the board can be rotated inside it.

tools.name: STEP / Parasolid export
tools.description: Writes the board — outline, copper if requested, and every 3D body — as a STEP or Parasolid assembly for the mechanical CAD package. Export options control which components are included, whether to export at the component or board level, and the coordinate origin, which must match what the MCAD engineer expects.
tools.usage: File > Export > STEP 3D… / Parasolid…

parameters.name: Component export
parameters.description: Which components and 3D bodies are written, and whether simple extrusions are included.

parameters.name: Origin
parameters.description: Whether the export is referenced to the board origin or the absolute origin.

tools.example: File > Export > STEP 3D > include all components > board origin > board.step, and send it to mechanical for the enclosure fit check.

tools.name: 3D clearance and collision checking
tools.description: Detects interference in 3D. The Component Clearance design rule can be configured to check 3D bodies rather than 2D courtyards, giving real height-aware clearance; View Configuration's 3D settings highlight colliding bodies; and the 3D view can be sectioned to inspect a specific area. It is what catches a capacitor fouling a heatsink before the prototype is built.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Placement > Component Clearance (check mode: 3D bodies); View Configuration > View Options > Show 3D Bodies / highlight collisions; then Tools > Design Rule Check
tools.example: Set the Component Clearance rule to 3D checking with a 0.5 mm gap, run the batch DRC, and review the reported collisions in the 3D view.

tools.name: MCAD CoDesigner
tools.description: The bidirectional link between Altium Designer and mechanical CAD (SolidWorks, Autodesk Inventor, PTC Creo, Siemens NX, Autodesk Fusion, Onshape). Board shape, component placement, holes, keepouts and 3D bodies are exchanged as reviewable change sets through Altium 365, so ECAD and MCAD stay synchronised instead of trading STEP files.
tools.usage: View > Panels > MCAD CoDesigner (requires the CoDesigner extension in Altium and the matching MCAD plug-in)
tools.example: MCAD CoDesigner > Push to MCAD; the mechanical engineer adjusts the outline and pushes back; review and accept the change in Altium.
tools.notes: Requires an Altium 365 workspace and the corresponding plug-in installed in the MCAD tool; it is not a file-based exchange.

tools.name: Rigid-flex board regions
tools.description: Divides the board shape into regions, each assigned its own stackup from the Layer Stack Manager, so a design can be rigid in some areas and flexible in others. Split Board Region and the region properties define the boundaries, and the 3D view renders the assembled shape once bending lines are added.
tools.usage: Design > Board Shape > Split Board Region; assign a stackup per region in the Layer Stack Manager; Board Planning Mode (1) to edit regions
tools.example: Press 1 for Board Planning Mode, Design > Board Shape > Split Board Region to carve out the flex tail, and assign it the 2-layer flex stackup.

tools.name: Bending lines
tools.description: Defines where and how far a flex region folds. A bending line carries an angle, radius and the region it moves, and the 3D view then shows the board in its folded state so clearance in the assembled product can be checked. The bend radius is also checked against the flex stackup's minimum.
tools.usage: Board Planning Mode (1) > Place > Bending Line; set angle and radius in the Properties panel
tools.example: Place a bending line across the flex tail, set 90° with a 3 mm radius, switch to 3D and confirm the connector reaches its mating part.

tools.name: Embedded Board Array (panelisation)
tools.description: Places one or more instances of another PCB project inside the current board, which is how an assembly panel or a multi-design array is built in Altium. Row and column counts, spacings and rotation are set in the object's properties, and the panel inherits the source board's data so it updates when the source changes.
tools.usage: Place > Embedded Board Array/Panelize…; set the source PCB project, row/column count and spacing in the Properties panel

parameters.name: Row Spacing / Column Spacing / Row Margin / Column Margin
parameters.description: Pitch and border of the array.

parameters.name: Rotation / Mirror
parameters.description: Per-instance orientation, used for alternating panels.

tools.example: New blank PcbDoc sized to the panel, Place > Embedded Board Array > source sensor.PcbDoc, 3 columns x 2 rows, 2 mm spacing; add the rails, fiducials and tooling holes around it.

tools.name: PCB Library Editor
tools.description: Creates and edits footprints in a .PcbLib. A footprint is built from pads, primitives on the silkscreen and mechanical layers, a courtyard, a 3D body and the footprint's own name and description. The PCB Library panel lists the footprints and their primitives, and supports placing, renaming, copying and reporting on them.
tools.usage: File > New > Library > PCB Library; View > Panels > PCB Library; Tools > New Blank Footprint
tools.example: Tools > New Blank Footprint 'QFN-32_5x5', place 32 pads and the thermal pad, draw the assembly outline on Mechanical 13 and the courtyard on the courtyard layer, add a 3D body.

tools.name: IPC Compliant Footprint Wizard
tools.description: Generates a footprint from the component's package dimensions using the IPC-7351 calculations, with Least/Nominal/Most material density levels. Entering the datasheet's body, lead and pitch dimensions (and tolerances) produces correct pad sizes, courtyard, assembly outline and silkscreen without hand calculation. The Batch variant generates many footprints from a spreadsheet.
tools.usage: PCB Library Editor > Tools > IPC Compliant Footprint Wizard… / IPC Compliant Footprints Batch Generator…

parameters.name: Component type
parameters.description: BGA, CHIP, CFP, DFN, LCC, MELF, MOLDED, PLCC, PSON, QFN, QFP, SOIC, SOP, SOT, SOD, WIRE WRAP and more.

parameters.name: Density level
parameters.description: Least (L), Nominal (N) or Most (M) material condition, setting the toe/heel/side fillets.

parameters.name: Mechanical layers / courtyard
parameters.description: Which layers the assembly outline, courtyard and component centre are placed on.

tools.example: Tools > IPC Compliant Footprint Wizard > QFN > body 5x5 mm, 32 pins, 0.5 mm pitch, thermal pad 3.3 mm, density Nominal > Finish.
tools.notes: Prefer this over the generic Footprint Wizard: it produces IPC-compliant courtyards and assembly outlines that the placement rules and 3D checks rely on.

tools.name: Footprint Wizard (generic)
tools.description: The older, pattern-based wizard: pick a package family (DIP, SOP, BGA, capacitors, diodes, resistors, edge connectors, leadless chip carriers, quad packs, pin arrays), then enter pad sizes, pitch and row counts directly. Useful for connectors and non-standard parts where you have the pad geometry rather than IPC package dimensions.
tools.usage: PCB Library Editor > Tools > Footprint Wizard…
tools.example: Tools > Footprint Wizard > Dual In-line Package > pad 1.6/0.8 mm, pitch 2.54 mm, 8 pins, row spacing 7.62 mm.

tools.name: Place Pad (PCB library)
tools.description: Creates a pad. Properties cover the designator, layer (top/bottom/multi-layer), shape per layer (Round, Rectangular, Octagonal, Rounded Rectangle with a corner radius, or a custom Region-based shape), size, hole (round, square or slot with a rotation), plating, and the mask expansion overrides. Multi-layer pads with a hole are through-hole pins; single-layer pads are SMD.
tools.usage: Place > Pad (P,P) in the PCB Library or PCB editor; Tab to edit before placing

parameters.name: Shape / Size (X,Y) per layer
parameters.description: Top, Middle and Bottom stack can differ when 'Full Stack' or 'Top-Middle-Bottom' mode is selected.

parameters.name: Hole Size / Hole Type
parameters.description: Round, Square or Slot with length and rotation.

parameters.name: Plated
parameters.description: Distinguishes a PTH from an NPTH mounting hole.

parameters.name: Paste/Solder Mask Expansion
parameters.description: Per-pad override of the mask rules.

tools.example: P,P, Tab, Layer Multi-Layer, Shape Round 1.6 mm, Hole Round 0.9 mm, Plated, Designator 1, place at the origin.

tools.name: Courtyard and assembly outlines
tools.description: The non-copper outlines that make placement checking and documentation work: the courtyard (component keep-out boundary, used by the Component Clearance rule), the assembly outline (true body outline used on assembly drawings), and the component centre/designator. Each is drawn on a mechanical layer whose layer type is set accordingly in the Layer Stack Manager.
tools.usage: Draw on the mechanical layers typed as Courtyard, Assembly and Component Center; the IPC wizard creates them automatically
tools.example: Draw the courtyard 0.25 mm outside the maximum body on the Courtyard Top layer so the Component Clearance rule has something to check.
tools.notes: If footprints have no courtyard, component clearance checking silently falls back to bounding boxes and gives misleading results.

tools.name: PCB Library panel
tools.description: Lists the footprints in the open .PcbLib with their pad and primitive counts, plus the components in the design that use them. It supports placing a footprint, renaming, deleting, copying between libraries and reporting, and it is where Update PCB is launched from.
tools.usage: View > Panels > PCB Library (PCB Library editor)
tools.example: PCB Library panel > right-click 'SOIC-8' > Update PCB With All to push a pad-size fix into every board that uses it.

tools.name: Update PCB / Update PCB With All (library)
tools.description: Pushes a footprint change from the library into the open board documents through an ECO, so existing placements pick up corrected pads, silkscreen or 3D bodies. Without it, editing the library has no effect on designs, because each board holds its own copy of the footprint.
tools.usage: PCB Library Editor > Tools > Update PCB With Current Footprint / Update PCB With All Footprints
tools.example: Fix the thermal pad size in company.PcbLib > Tools > Update PCB With Current Footprint > review the ECO > Execute Changes.

tools.name: Footprint report and library reports
tools.description: Reports on library content: the component report for a single footprint (pads, layers, dimensions), the library report listing every footprint with its primitive counts and an optional image, and the library-versus-design comparison that finds footprints in the design that no longer match the library.
tools.usage: PCB Library Editor > Reports > Component / Library Report / Component Rule Check
tools.example: Reports > Library Report > tick 'Include component parameters' and 'Add images' > generate a PDF catalogue of the company library.

tools.name: Component Rule Check (library)
tools.description: Checks the footprints in a library for common defects: duplicate pad designators, missing pad designators, floating copper, overlapping primitives, un-named footprints and footprints with no pads. Running it before publishing a library catches the problems that would otherwise surface as DRC noise on every board.
tools.usage: PCB Library Editor > Reports > Component Rule Check…
tools.example: Reports > Component Rule Check > tick Duplicate Pads, Missing Pad Names, Offset Component Reference > OK, and fix the listed footprints.

tools.name: Set Reference (footprint origin)
tools.description: Sets the footprint's origin, which is the point the pick-and-place machine and the placement commands use. Options are Pin 1, Center or a chosen Location. An origin that is not at the body centre or pin 1 produces pick-and-place data that the assembler has to correct by hand.
tools.usage: PCB Library Editor > Edit > Set Reference > Pin 1 / Center / Location
tools.example: Edit > Set Reference > Center for a QFN so the centroid data matches the body centre.

tools.name: Board Planning Mode
tools.description: A dedicated 2D mode for working on the board's physical definition rather than its circuitry: board shape and regions, layer stack assignment per region, bending lines and split lines. It hides the routing so the mechanical structure can be edited without interference.
tools.usage: View > Board Planning Mode (1)
tools.example: Press 1, split the board into rigid and flex regions, place the bending lines, then press 3 to see the folded assembly.

tools.name: Layer Stack Regions (rigid-flex stackups)
tools.description: In a rigid-flex design the Layer Stack Manager holds several named stackups — for example 'Rigid 4-layer' and 'Flex 2-layer' — and each board region is assigned one. Substacks share the layers they have in common, so a trace can run continuously from the rigid section onto the flex tail.
tools.usage: Design > Layer Stack Manager > Board Region / stackup dropdown; assign in Board Planning Mode
tools.example: Create stackups 'RIGID' and 'FLEX' in the Layer Stack Manager, then assign FLEX to the tail region in Board Planning Mode.

tools.name: Mounting holes and non-plated holes
tools.description: Mechanical holes are placed as pads with a hole and plating turned off (NPTH) or as plated pads with a net (PTH tied to GND for chassis grounding). Using pads rather than drawn circles means the holes appear in the drill file and are checked by the Hole Size and Hole To Hole rules.
tools.usage: Place > Pad with Plated unticked; or place a mounting-hole footprint from the library
tools.example: Place > Pad, Layer Multi-Layer, Hole 3.2 mm, pad 3.2 mm, Plated unticked — an M3 clearance hole that appears in the NPTH drill file.
tools.notes: A circle drawn on a mechanical layer produces no drill data; the fabricator will not drill it.

tools.name: Fiducials
tools.description: Optical alignment targets for the assembly machine: an exposed copper dot with a solder-mask opening around it, placed as a footprint so it carries no net and appears correctly on the paste and mask layers. Global fiducials go on the board (typically three, asymmetrically placed) and local fiducials next to fine-pitch parts.
tools.usage: Place a fiducial footprint from the library; exclude it from the BOM in the component's properties
tools.example: Place three 1 mm copper / 2 mm mask fiducials at asymmetric board corners and mark them 'Exclude From BOM'.

tools.name: Dimensions (PCB)
tools.description: Dimensioning objects for the fabrication drawing: Linear, Angular, Radial, Leader, Datum, Baseline, Center, Origin and Linear Diameter. They are placed on a mechanical layer and follow the objects they are attached to. For a full drawing set, Draftsman is generally preferred because its dimensions update with the board.
tools.usage: Place > Dimension > Linear / Angular / Radial / Leader / Datum / Baseline / Center / Linear Diameter
tools.example: Place > Dimension > Linear across the board width on the Fab Notes mechanical layer.

tools.name: Signal Integrity analysis
tools.description: Altium's built-in reflection and crosstalk analyser. Using the layer stack, the nets' geometry and IBIS-derived or generic pin models, it screens the board for overshoot, undershoot, impedance and flight-time violations against the Signal Integrity design rules, and can open a reflection or crosstalk waveform for a selected net with a terminator advisor.
tools.usage: Tools > Signal Integrity… (requires Supply Nets rules and component SI models)
tools.example: Set the Supply Nets rule (+3V3, GND), Tools > Signal Integrity, select the clock net > Reflections > add a series terminator in the advisor and re-analyse.
tools.notes: Accuracy depends on real IBIS models; with generic models it is a screening tool, not a sign-off simulator.

tools.name: IBIS model import
tools.description: Loads a vendor IBIS (.ibs) file and maps its pin models to a component's pins so that signal-integrity analysis uses the real buffer characteristics. Imported models become the component's Signal Integrity model and are stored with the library component.
tools.usage: Tools > Signal Integrity > Model Assignments > Import IBIS…; or add a Signal Integrity model to the library component
tools.example: Import the MCU's .ibs file, map the LVCMOS33 output model to the clock pin, then re-run the SI screening.

tools.name: Board Information report
tools.description: Summarises the board: dimensions, layer count, primitive counts by type and layer, pad and via counts by hole size, net count, component counts by side, and the annular ring and hole size extremes. It is the quick sanity check before quoting or releasing a board and is also available as a Report output in an OutJob.
tools.usage: Reports > Board Information; also Reports > Board Stack Report
tools.example: Reports > Board Information > Report > confirm the smallest hole and thinnest track are within the chosen fabricator's capability.
